What's It Like?
Guardians of the Galaxy was an amazing surprise. Its approach to storytelling, weaving dialogue into the gameplay through banter, huddles and story choices, makes the adventure genuinely engaging and delivers some laugh-out-loud moments along the way. The slick and stylish combat system is incredibly satisfying, while the gorgeous visuals deliver some of the most jaw-dropping set pieces I’ve seen on the Switch 2. Sure, there were moments where the framerate faltered and a couple of bugs along the way, but these do little to get in the way of what is an outstanding adventure.
Nintendo Switch 2 FULL REVIEW
Nov 2, 2026
90
NintendoWorldReport
I think Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy is absolutely worth playing, but the Switch 2-exclusive features are not compelling enough to recommend over existing next-gen versions. That’s not to say you shouldn’t buy it on Switch 2; if that’s your jam, go nuts, but don’t expect anything absolutely game-changing. Now, for me, the fact that I can play this game on an airplane or in bed is a priceless feature. You don’t have to give me new skins–the fact that it works in Handheld mode alone is worth the price of admission. That said, you should play this game however you can, whether on Switch 2 or something else.
Nintendo Switch 2 FULL REVIEW

Nintendo Life
Guardians of the Galaxy was criminally overlooked when it first came out on other platforms. This single-player adventure is full of heart with equally fun gameplay to match. It’s also a shame that the disastrous Cloud version on the first Switch cast a large shadow on an otherwise stellar release. But those dark days are over. If you can stomach some performance issues, this is one bright and resonating story you’ll want to experience at least once. Without the need of a constant internet connection, you can take Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition outside in the sun, literally.
Nintendo Switch 2 FULL REVIEW
Nov 3, 2026
70
Nintendo Insider
It’s important to know what you’re getting into with Marvel’s Guardians of the Galaxy: Encore Edition on Nintendo Switch 2, however. The handheld performance is quite rough at times, and as a whole the presentation is a little underwhelming compared to some of the better Switch 2 ports out there. If you don’t have another option to play the game and can handle some framerate issues (especially in handheld mode), then this will do the job. The new costumes are neither here nor there, but the gyro aiming and mouse controls are at least a nice add. This is a really good game that I have a lot of fondness for, and I’m glad we have a non-streaming option on the Switch 2 now. I just wish the performance was a little better.
Nintendo Switch 2 FULL REVIEW
Nov 2, 2026
60
Multiplayer.it
As might have been expected, the level of detail drops precipitously—perhaps even more than anticipated. This might be acceptable if the loss in visual impact were compensated for by better performance, but unfortunately, that is not the case. When you undock the console and the graphics take a nabbing hit, you also—and perhaps most noticeably—encounter a stuttering frame rate, especially during cutscenes and particularly crowded combat sequences. Not only are you forced to look at highly detailed characters like Rocket—who, in wide shots, end up looking more like household cleaning tools than alien creatures—but you also have to endure constant hitches and stutters in the game's visual fluidity. This makes the title, if not entirely unplayable, certainly far from enjoyable—especially considering that the game relies heavily on the wonder of its visuals to foster an emotional connection with the player.
Nintendo Switch 2 FULL REVIEW
